H: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up about 75% of all normal matter.
It is the only element that can exist without neutrons.
He: Helium is the second most abundant element, yet it is so light that Earth's gravity cannot hold it, and it escapes into space.
It becomes a superfluid near absolute zero, defying gravity and creeping up the sides of containers.
Li: Lithium is the lightest metal and can float on water.
It is widely used in rechargeable batteries for smartphones and electric vehicles.
Be: Beryllium is incredibly stiff and lightweight, making it ideal for aerospace applications.
It is highly toxic to humans if its dust is inhaled.
B: Boron is crucial for plant growth but can be toxic in large amounts.
It is used in flares and fireworks to produce a vibrant green color.
C: Carbon is the foundation of all known life on Earth.
It can exist as both the softest mineral (graphite) and one of the hardest (diamond).
N: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.
Liquid nitrogen is used for freezing and transporting food, and for cryopreservation.
O: Oxygen is highly reactive and forms compounds with almost all other elements.
Liquid oxygen is pale blue and highly paramagnetic, meaning it can be attracted by a magnet.
F: Fluorine is the most electronegative and reactive of all elements.
It is added to public water supplies and toothpaste to prevent tooth decay.
Ne: Neon glows reddish-orange in a vacuum discharge tube, giving us the classic neon sign.
It is completely inert and has no known stable chemical compounds.
